role: EnchantmentHelper.buildEnchantmentList and addRandomEnchantment for loot books and enchanted trade and mob equipment items: the item's enchantability, the level draws, mapEnchantmentData rebuilt as a Java 8 HashMap so WeightedRandom walks its values in the same bucket order, the repeat loop with canApplyTogether, and ItemEnchantedBook's StoredEnchantments tag rendered as NBT.

structs.name: hashmap
structs.java: java.util.HashMap<Integer, EnchantmentData> as mapEnchantmentData builds it (table size, threshold, tail-appended chains)

gpu: functions hm_init, hm_put, hm_resize: the mapEnchantmentData HashMap holds its buckets and entries in fixed arrays (HM_MAX 64: one node per enchantment, at most 32 buckets reached) and allocates nothing (lane/querybounds, TM-06)
line 141-142 and 176-177, functions hm_put and hm_resize: linear chain walks to append at the tail (index-linked chains, container order reproduced deliberately)

line 305, function build_enchantment_list: the repeat loop runs while nextInt(50) <= var11 with var11 halving; once var11 is 0 it continues with probability 1/50 per step (unbounded in principle, as in Java)
line 349-374, functions book_tag, add_random_enchantment_book and add_random_enchantment_tag: nbt tree allocation and malloc'd rendered text
notes: The header comment says the HashMap lives in java_hashmap.c; in this file it is implemented inline (hm_*). Java removes conflicting entries from the map permanently each round; the port re-filters all candidates against every pick so far, which selects the same survivors in the same map order. Item enchantability for armor is a per-item-id switch (not in items.h). Callers: loot.c (chest books), trades.c (priest trades), hostiles.c, hostiles_skeleton.c, hostiles_spider.c and spawning.c (mob equipment). No test calls these functions directly; the listed tests were chosen because their subjects call enchant.c (not verified that each covers an enchanted path). The enchanting table itself is switched off (world.conf enchanting=off).
